books.section: C. The Lower South and the West Indies

options.text: The average sugar grower held 115 enslaved workers, whose labor made the sugar.

options.misconception: Big exports are what the historian must explain — they support his claim, they do not challenge it.
options.text: Barbados exported about 50 million pounds of sugar a year, more than Virginia's tobacco.

options.misconception: Virginia's tobacco says nothing about where Barbados's wealth came from.
options.text: Virginia exported more than 35 million pounds of tobacco, nearly as much as Barbados.

options.misconception: Their wealth is the fact to explain — it does not say whether soil or labor produced it.
options.text: Sugar planters were four times as wealthy as Virginians, and their wealth came from sugar.

rationales.A: Soil does not harvest sugar — 115 enslaved workers per grower is the labor that turned the soil into wealth.
rationales.B: Big exports are what the historian must explain — they support his claim, they do not challenge it.
rationales.C: Virginia's tobacco says nothing about where Barbados's wealth came from.
rationales.D: Their wealth is the fact to explain — it does not say whether soil or labor produced it.
rationales.general:
1. Name the claim. Fertile soil made the sugar planters rich.
2. Ask what soil cannot do alone. It cannot plant, cut, and boil sugar — hands do that.
3. Find the hands. One hundred fifteen enslaved workers per grower, on an island three-fourths enslaved.
Remember: when a claim credits the land, look for the labor — ask whose hands did the work.

source: original; data table drawn from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 4
stem: A historian argues that the wealth of Barbados's sugar planters came mainly from the island's fertile soil. Which evidence from the table best challenges that claim?

stimulus.text:
| Sugar in Barbados and tobacco in Virginia, about 1700 |
|---|---|
| Barbados sugar | About 50 million pounds exported in a year |
| Virginia tobacco | More than 35 million pounds exported in a year |
| Enslaved people, Barbados | About three-fourths of the population |
| Enslaved people, Virginia | Less than one-fourth of the population |
| Average sugar grower | 115 enslaved workers |
| Wealth of sugar planters | About four times that of Virginia tobacco planters |
